name: sec-audit
description: v1.36 least-privilege + incremental UX: --sarif=new emits only findings a run introduced (NEW/REGRESSED) for PR checks, with the GitHub-baselining rule documented so a new-mode log is never uploaded from the default branch (it would mass-close carried alerts); an accepted-risk register at <state_home>/accepted.json turns fingerprint-matched findings into ACCEPTED — expiry mandatory, CRITICAL capped at 30 days per acceptance and anchored at min(accepted, today) so no future-dated entry can extend it, never suppressing FIXED or REGRESSED, never removing a finding or shrinking total_open, and emitted as SARIF suppressions[] rather than dropped so an accepted risk stays auditable; --feeds-only re-checks dependency advisories with no code lane (nothing can be marked FIXED, run history records mode: feeds) and stays quiet when nothing moved while still appending its history line; SKILL.md 1.5.1 publishes the history.jsonl consumer contract; and cve-enricher, dep-diff-analyst and sec-expert lose an unused WebFetch grant they never invoked. v1.32 closes the loop: an audit of code that has not changed still surfaces vulnerabilities that BECAME known since the last run, while cutting redundant feed I/O. A new `AdvisoryCache` in cve_enricher caches per-advisory detail documents by id under a 7-day TTL in `<state_home>/advisory-cache.json` — but the OSV `querybatch` discovery call is NEVER cached, because it is precisely the 'did this unchanged version become vulnerable overnight?' probe; contract-check greps for any attempt to cache it. Measured live on 3 packages carrying 79 advisories: 82 requests cold, 3 warm (96% fewer) with an identical vulnerability set. A corrupt cache is discarded with a warning and the run proceeds at full cost — a damaged cache must never be able to hide an advisory. `deltas.py` gains three feed-driven classes: NEW (feed-driven) for an advisory newly returned for a package whose version did NOT change (rendered with a mandatory `(unchanged)` marker, since the reader's first instinct is 'what did I change?' and the answer is nothing), ESCALATED for a already-known advisory added to CISA KEV or crossing an EPSS scoring band, and WITHDRAWN for an advisory the feeds no longer return — reported as withdrawn and explicitly NOT as fixed, since nothing about the code changed. The offline drill gains the dangerous case: offline WITH a warm cache reports every package UNKNOWN (stale), never SAFE, so the absence of a fresh check can never read as a clean bill of health. v1.31 also answers the version question directly. New `versions.py` implements PEP 440, SemVer 2.0.0 §11, Go/RubyGems/Maven and dpkg §5.6.12 comparison (tilde rule included) plus the OSV event algorithm — introduced/fixed/last_affected/limit, `introduced: "0"`, and `versions[]` OR `ranges[]` (the spec ORs them; neither takes precedence) — and computes, per package, VULNERABLE / SAFE / UNKNOWN, the vulnerable ranges, and the minimum safe upgrade (absolute and within-major). Only advisory-named fixed versions are ever proposed, filtered to the package under evaluation: a live cross-check caught GHSA-6c3j-c64m-qhgq (a jQuery advisory that also lists Django) contributing jquery-rails' 4.3.4 as Django's 'safe' upgrade — now correctly 4.2.26. GIT ranges are skipped as unevaluable without repo access, but only taint the verdict when an entry has nothing else evaluable. UNKNOWN — never SAFE — is returned for an offline feed, a declared range, an unsupported ecosystem, or an approximate comparison, and a SAFE verdict is always qualified as 'no advisory in the consulted feeds affects this exact version', never 'this version is secure'. cve-enricher now captures the full `affected[]` projection and attaches the verdict; the report gains Dependency-version-safety and Program-&-runtime-versions sections, each splitting Vulnerable / Verified safe / Unknown with every package in exactly one table. Verified live against 5 known-vulnerable packages: all 5 computed min_safe values re-verify clean. v1.31 replaces the LLM-produced dependency list with a deterministic one. New `depinv.py` parses RESOLVED LOCKFILES first and declared manifests only as a fallback across ten OSV-native ecosystems (PyPI poetry/uv/Pipfile/requirements, npm package-lock v1+v2/v3 with transitive-vs-direct detection, yarn classic+berry, pnpm, Cargo.lock, go.sum/go.mod, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, gradle.lockfile/pom.xml, packages.lock.json, Podfile.lock, Package.resolved), labelling every package `lockfile` / `pinned` / `declared` / `unparsed` — only the first two are exact enough to support a version-safety claim, and a declared RANGE is recorded verbatim rather than resolved into a version that was never installed. A malformed lockfile degrades to `unparsed` and is reported, never silently dropped. New `programs.py` extracts the half a lockfile never covers — base images, apt/apk pins, CI action pins and toolchain pins — under two honesty rules: a floating tag (`FROM node:20`, `@v4`) is recorded with a null version and `pinned: false` because it is not a version, and an entry with no OSV ecosystem is emitted with `ecosystem: null` so it renders UNKNOWN rather than implying the feeds cleared it. SKILL.md §4 makes depinv the source of truth with sec-expert's `__dep_inventory__` demoted to a union fallback (deterministic parser wins a version conflict; the discrepancy is surfaced, never silently reconciled). `changeset.py` gains dependency + program deltas (added / removed / version_changed / unchanged plus a `requery` set), detected independently of file hashes so a transitive bump inside a regenerated lockfile is never missed. Verified against real portfolio projects: 272 crates, 59 Go modules, 118 npm packages. v1.30 makes re-audits incremental by default: when the state home already holds a baseline, only the changed surface is re-analysed and everything else is carried forward with provenance. `fingerprint.py` gives each finding a line-independent identity (sha256 over origin/tool/rule/file/CWE/normalized evidence — a finding pushed 40 lines down by an unrelated edit is the same finding) and hashes the tree into a content-addressed manifest that reuses inventory.py's SKIP_DIRS so the manifest and the scanners can never disagree about what 'the tree' is. `changeset.py` decides per lane re-run or carry, with a reason string that reaches the report; it is fail-safe by construction — a lane is skipped only when nothing it looks at changed AND its definition digest (lane JSON + runner agent + runner.py, or for sec-expert the whole reference-pack tree) is identical AND its last run ended `ok` AND it is inside the 30-day staleness TTL, while unknown lanes, missing digests, degraded runs and the always-on lanes (secrets, whose trufflehog pass scans git history; dast, whose target is a live instance) always re-run. `deltas.py` classifies every finding NEW / REVERIFIED / CARRIED / FIXED / REGRESSED under three safety invariants — FIXED requires the producing lane to have re-run AND finished ok, a degraded lane carries with `stale: true` and fixes nothing, and a deleted file resolves without a re-run — and enforces a conservation law (every baseline finding comes out as exactly one of carried/reverified/fixed, else exit 5) so a finding can never be silently dropped. SKILL.md gains §2.5 Changeset and §4.9 Merge & classify (before §5, so carried and fresh findings take one identical scoring pass) plus a §3.0 incremental dispatch filter keeping 'carried' distinct from 'out of scope' and 'excluded by the caller'; the report gains Changes-since-last-audit and Fixed-since-last-audit sections and a per-finding Status line whose CARRIED wording must state 'not re-verified this run'. New `--full` forces a rebaseline. Five new hermetic suites incl. a two-run incremental-e2e whose centrepiece is the conservation assertion. v1.29 moves every sec-audit artifact out of the audited project and into that project's portfolio home: a new deterministic `scripts/secaudit/statehome.py` resolves `<portfolio_root>/<area>/<name>/security/` from `~/.claude/projects-registry.yaml` (longest-prefix match, so a subdirectory of a registered project resolves to it; `enabled: false` entries ignored; dev-root inference and a deterministic `_adhoc/<slug>` fallback behind a one-time confirmation; `--state-dir` override for an unmounted vault or CI), and `scripts/secaudit/statestore.py` owns a schema-versioned `audit-state.json` (atomic tmp+rename write), an append-only `history.jsonl`, and a 50-entry in-state `runs[]` cap. The report, the `--sarif` log, and a new `latest.md` pointer are written to `<state_home>/reports/`; report-writer's output discipline now FORBIDS writing into the audited tree rather than mandating it, and contract-check fails on any surviving in-target report path. A corrupt or future-schema state file is a hard error, never a silent empty skeleton — discarding a damaged baseline would report every carried finding as NEW and make fixed findings vanish; the error names `--full`, the deliberate way to rebaseline. New `--full` and `--state-dir` command flags (flags, not lane names), a new SKILL.md §1.5 State home section with the exit-3 no-fallback rule, run provenance (State home / Run id / Previous run, with an explicit `none — first audit` marker) in the report metadata, and two new hermetic suites (script-statehome, script-statestore) wired into CI. Consequence tracked as BL-003: `planning:project-maturity`'s `auto:repo:sec-audit-report-*.md` Security-axis detector no longer fires, since reports are no longer written into the repo. v1.28 hardens the plugin's own least-privilege posture (CWE-693): the 19 engine-backed runner agents, the 4 pipeline agents (cve-enricher/report-writer/sec-expert/dep-diff-analyst), and the `/sec-audit` orchestrator command now scope their `Bash` tool grant to a per-tool allowlist (`Bash(python3:*)`, `Bash(date:*)`, etc.) instead of a blanket `Bash`, so a prompt-injected agent reading an untrusted target tree cannot run arbitrary commands. A new `tests/contract-check.sh` gate rejects any bare `Bash` grant in agent/command frontmatter. The 6 host-OS-gated runners (ios/macos/windows/ai-tools/linux/netcfg) are tracked for the same treatment in backlog BL-002 pending live permission-matcher verification. v1.27 adds a new `php` lane (§3.30): PHP / WordPress source review via `phpcs` (PHP_CodeSniffer) run with the WordPress Coding Standards security sniffs — EscapeOutput (unescaped output → XSS, CWE-79), NonceVerification (missing CSRF nonce, CWE-352), ValidatedSanitizedInput (unvalidated/unsanitized request input, CWE-20), and PreparedSQL/PreparedSQLPlaceholders (unprepared SQL, CWE-89) — mapped through the deterministic runner engine (the JSON `files` object is iterated by value with the path key exposed as `_parent._key`, `messages[]` flattened, sniff `source`->CWE lookup). `inventory.py` fires the lane on a `*.php` source or `composer.json`, disambiguating a `["wordpress"]` sub-shape (wp-config.php / `Theme Name:` style.css / add_action functions.php) from `["generic"]`. WordPress is thereby promoted from a coverage-gap fingerprint to a covered lane; the fingerprint entry is retained but narrowed to the non-WordPress (Laravel/Symfony) subset whose deep taint analysis still needs a Composer-autoload-rooted tool. New `no-php-source` target-shape skip reason (31 total); command lane list 25->26; phpcs added to the contract-check origin-isolation matrix + a v1.27-symmetry test; two new detective packs (php/wordpress.md, php/php-web.md). v1.26 adds a new `c-cpp` lane (§3.29): C/C++ source memory-safety review via `cppcheck` (data-flow static analyzer — buffer overruns CWE-788/120, memory leaks CWE-401, use-after-free CWE-416, uninitialised reads; `--xml` with per-error cwe attributes) + `flawfinder` (lexical banned-libc-function scanner — strcpy/gets/sprintf→CWE-120, system→CWE-78, printf-format→CWE-134; `--sarif`), both mapped through the deterministic runner engine. `inventory.py` fires the lane on a C/C++ SOURCE file (a header alone does not — vendored/JNI `*.h` is ubiquitous and would false-positive). A new additive `regex` field-transform in the engine extracts CWE from flawfinder's message text (no other lane's parity changes). The former `cpp` coverage-gap fingerprint is retired (it is now a covered lane); new `no-c-source` target-shape skip reason (30 total); command lane list 24->25; cppcheck/flawfinder added to the contract-check origin-isolation matrix + a v1.26-symmetry test. v1.25 adds docker-compose misconfiguration scanning to the `virt` lane: a third tool, `kics` (Checkmarx, Apache-2.0), runs `kics scan --type DockerCompose` over `docker-compose.y(a)ml`/`compose.y(a)ml` files, mapping its bundled dockerCompose query set (privileged containers CWE-250, shared host PID/IPC/network namespaces CWE-668, docker-socket bind-mounts CWE-284, unrestricted capabilities, no-new-privileges disabled CWE-732, unbounded resource limits CWE-770) to the finding schema via the deterministic runner engine (queries[]→files[] flatten, severity/cwe/file/line map; origin `virt`, tool `kics`). `--type DockerCompose` scopes kics to compose files so it never re-reports Dockerfile findings hadolint already owns. `inventory.py` now fires `virt` on a compose file alone (name-glob + services:/version: content grep), so a compose-only project with no Dockerfile is no longer invisible to the lane. New detective pack `virt/compose-hardening.md`, new `no-compose-file` target-shape skip reason (23 total), kics added to the virt tool whitelist + all foreign-lane isolation sets + a v1.25-symmetry contract test. v1.24 widens portfolio coverage without a new tool lane: four new uncovered-technology fingerprints (Garmin Connect IQ / Monkey C `monkey.jungle`+`manifest.xml`+`*.mc`; OpenWrt package feed Makefiles with `include $(TOPDIR)/rules.mk`; F-Droid repository servers via fdroidserver `config.yml`; Homebrew taps via `Casks/*.rb`/`Formula/*.rb`) are added to `references/uncovered-tech-fingerprints.md` so the §2 second pass surfaces them as Coverage-gap suggestions (Connect IQ and the OpenWrt package layer were previously invisible to that pass entirely). The `secrets` lane's key-material globs widen to `*.jks`/`*.keystore`/`*.der`/`developer_key.*`/`keystore.p12` (committed signing keystores / PKCS#8 developer keys, CWE-798) and gain an fdroidserver plaintext-keystore-password pattern (`keystorepass:`/`keypass:` literals, CWE-256); a new `supply-chain/homebrew-tap.md` detective pack covers `sha256 :no_check` (CWE-494), cleartext download URLs (CWE-319), unpinned moving-tag URLs (CWE-829), and arbitrary postflight/preflight install Ruby (CWE-506). v1.23 makes sec-audit usable at PR time: `--sarif` emits a GitHub-code-scanning-compatible SARIF 2.1.0 log beside the markdown report (deterministic `scripts/secaudit/sarif.py`, the pipeline's first machine-readable deliverable; severity→level, CVSS/score→security-severity, sentinels filtered, secrets never surfaced), and `--diff[=ref]` scopes the whole review to changed files (`scripts/secaudit/diffscope.py` computes the changed set; `inventory.py`/`runner.py` gain `--files` scoping; runner now prunes `.git`/vendored dirs). v1.22 adds EPSS (FIRST.org exploit-probability) enrichment: `cve-enricher` batch-fetches EPSS scores (100 CVE ids/GET, only ids leave the machine) after the KEV pass and attaches `epss` / `epss_percentile` to every CVE; the §5 exploit sub-score becomes graded (KEV=20 / EPSS≥0.5=15 / EPSS≥0.1=10 / PoC=10 / else 0, max unchanged so buckets don't shift), and the report renders EPSS on each CVE line plus a Max-EPSS column. v1.21 adds the `secrets` lane — gitleaks (working-tree scan with `--redact`) + trufflehog (git-history scan with `--no-verification`, so no credential is ever tested against a live service) — detecting leaked credentials (CWE-798) across every project; gitleaks always scans the working tree while trufflehog scans git history when the target is a repo (else a `no-git-history` clean-skip). Evidence is always the redacted match, never the raw secret (enforced by a canary in the e2e). v1.21 also lands the project's own CI: a GitHub Actions workflow running the hermetic test suite (`tests/ci-local.sh`) on push/PR. v1.20 converts the `virt` lane to the deterministic runner engine via a new per-file pass/fail `validator` mode (exit-code → synthesized finding, with `line_regex` + `dedupe_by`) plus list-valued `applicable_glob` and multi-glob `{files:a|b}` support — hadolint maps with existing engine features and virt-xml-validate runs through the validator mode, so 16 of the runner lanes are now deterministic script-backed. The COVERAGE "still agent-backed" set is reclassified by benefit: planned-conversion (ai-tools — validator mode now exists, still needs a field `coalesce` op + a golden fixture), parked (linux — pending a table-parsing mode), and permanently agent-backed by design (macos/ios/windows host-OS-gated signing tools + netcfg config validators, where conversion saves no per-finding LLM cost). v1.19 adds the engine `cvss_band` transform and `input_format: xml` adapter, converting the rust (cargo-audit/deny/geiger) and android (mobsfscan/apkleaks/android-lint XML) lanes — 15 of the 22 runner lanes are now deterministic script-backed; the remaining 7 (ai-tools jq-validation, netcfg/virt validators, linux/macos/ios/windows command-output + host-OS-gated) stay LLM agents by design. v1.18 extends the v1.17 deterministic-runner engine with filter specs, nested/multi-source flatten, dict-iteration, and substring transforms, converting four more lanes (supply-chain, k8s, webext, webapp) to scripts — 13 of the runner lanes are now script-backed (only android/rust/ai-tools and the validator/desktop lanes remain LLM agents, by design). v1.17 moves the deterministic parts of the pipeline into stdlib-Python scripts under scripts/secaudit/ (no third-party deps): cve_enricher.py (OSV/NVD/GHSA/KEV + MAL- classification), score.py (the §5 prioritization rubric), inventory.py (the §2 file-glob/content-grep detection pre-pass), and a config-driven runner engine (runner.py + lanes/<lane>.json) that deterministically maps tool-native JSON to the finding schema for the sast, go, shell, ansible, gh-actions, python, iac, image, and dast lanes. Those agents become thin wrappers that run the script and apply a presentation-only polish (hybrid model), eliminating per-finding fabrication risk while preserving the JSONL/sentinel/origin contract (contract-check + drills + e2e unchanged). Lanes with multi-array or non-JSON tools (k8s, webext, webapp, supply-chain, android, rust, ai-tools, netcfg, virt, linux, macos, ios, windows) remain LLM runner agents. Cybersecurity review plugin covering web services, servers, browser extensions, Rust projects, Go projects, Python projects, Ansible playbooks, shell scripts (bash/sh/dash/ksh), networking-as-code (Tor torrc, WireGuard, sing-box, Xray), container image vulnerability scanning (trivy + grype on image tarballs / OCI layouts / SBOMs — the OSS-equivalent of Docker Scout's CVE surface without Docker-daemon / registry-pull dependencies), AI coding tool configuration (Claude Code plugins / agents / skills / commands / hooks / MCP servers, Cursor rules, Codex agents, OpenCode agents — covering prompt injection, tool poisoning (Invariant Labs / OWASP class), rug-pull supply-chain via unpinned npx/uvx, MCP server name shadowing / homoglyph in mcpServers keys, sampling-capability declaration, OAuth 2.0 + PKCE on HTTPS MCP per RFC 9700, confused-deputy blast-radius across multi-MCP setups, allowed-tools wildcards, hardcoded credentials, dangerous hooks, alwaysApply rule scoping, codex sandbox/approval policy — now also running mcp-scan inspect (Invariant Labs / Snyk Agent Scan) for tool-poisoning detection alongside jq for structural validation), Android apps, iOS apps, desktop Linux, desktop macOS, desktop Windows, Kubernetes manifests, Terraform/Pulumi IaC, GitHub Actions workflows, and virtualization / alternative-container-runtime configuration (Docker daemon, Podman / Quadlet, libvirt / QEMU / KVM, Apple Containers, UTM) via a pipelined twenty-seven-agent architecture (sec-expert, finding-triager, cve-enricher, sast-runner, dast-runner, webext-runner, rust-runner, android-runner, ios-runner, linux-runner, macos-runner, windows-runner, k8s-runner, iac-runner, gh-actions-runner, virt-runner, go-runner, shell-runner, python-runner, ansible-runner, netcfg-runner, image-runner, ai-tools-runner, webapp-runner, supply-chain-runner, dep-diff-analyst, report-writer). v1.16 adds the opt-in `--deep-deps` release-diff pass — the sonnet-pinned dep-diff-analyst agent fetches a flagged dependency's installed version N and prior version N-1 registry-natively (PyPI JSON API + npm registry, no pip/npm install), runs a bounded `diff -ruN`, and classifies the release benign / suspicious / malicious with diff-quoted evidence (origin `deep-deps`, tool `dep-diff`, a `verdict` field). Candidates come from the supply-chain lane + cve-enricher's MAL- array, capped at `deep_deps_max` (default 10); this is the point-in-time port of elastic/supply-chain-monitor's release-diff classification and the only signal that catches a compromised release of an otherwise-legitimate package. v1.15 adds the `supply-chain` lane — guarddog (Datadog, Apache-2.0; heuristic malicious-package scanner for PyPI + npm: install-time code execution, obfuscation, download-and-exec, exfiltration, typosquatting / dependency confusion) + osv-scanner (Google, Apache-2.0; full lockfile-graph resolution reporting OSV `MAL-` malicious-package advisories incl. transitives, filtered to MAL- only so CVEs are not double-reported) — detecting malicious dependencies (CWE-506 embedded malicious code, CWE-94 code injection, CWE-494 download-without-integrity, CWE-200 exfiltration, CWE-1357 typosquat/dependency-confusion, CWE-1007 trojan-source); paired with cve-enricher now classifying OSV `MAL-` + GHSA `type: malware` advisories (returned by its existing OSV/GHSA calls, no extra requests) into a per-package `malicious` array promoted to CRITICAL. Inspired by elastic/supply-chain-monitor's release-diff malware-classification approach, adapted point-in-time to the audited project's own dependency set. v1.14 adds the `webapp` lane — bearer (Apache-2.0; cross-language SAST tuned for OWASP Top 10 + data-flow tracking; supports JS/TS/Java/Ruby/PHP/Go/Python) + njsscan (MIT; Node.js-specific MobSF-family scanner) + brakeman (MIT; Rails-only deep SAST) — covering SQL injection (CWE-89), SSRF (CWE-918), XXE (CWE-611), path traversal (CWE-22), file upload (CWE-434), open redirect (CWE-601), SSTI (CWE-1336), mass assignment (CWE-915), IDOR / broken access control (CWE-639/CWE-285), prototype pollution (CWE-1321), command injection in web context (CWE-78), HTTP request smuggling / CORS misconfig / host-header injection (CWE-444/CWE-942/CWE-644), and insecure deserialization (CWE-502). v1.10 UX improvements: invocation defaults to current working directory when no path is supplied; inventory pass detects known-but-uncovered technologies and surfaces them as Coverage-gap suggestions in the report with model pinning — sonnet-grade code reasoning, haiku-grade CVE feed I/O and eight-lane tool dispatch. Multi-stack dispatch is the default: when a project satisfies ≥2 inventory keys (Tauri apps = Rust + webext + desktop OS; Flutter apps = Android + iOS; React-Native apps = Android + iOS + webext), all applicable runners dispatch in parallel and findings render in separate per-lane sections. The `/sec-audit` slash command accepts `--only=<lanes>` / `--skip=<lanes>` flags for selective dispatch; the final report includes a per-lane summary table and Lane-filter-applied metadata. Citation-grounded expertise across databases, frameworks, webservers (incl. Windows/IIS), proxies, frontend, browser extensions (Chrome MV3 + Firefox AMO), Rust/Cargo ecosystem + unsafe surface, Android (manifest + data + runtime), iOS (Info.plist + data + codesign), desktop Linux (systemd + sandboxing + packaging), desktop macOS (hardened runtime + TCC + .pkg/Sparkle), desktop Windows (PE hardening + Authenticode + AppLocker/WDAC + MSI/MSIX), auth, TLS, containers, secrets, and supply-chain — all primary-source-cited. Live CVE enrichment from NVD 2.0, OSV.dev (native for crates.io/Maven/NuGet/PyPI/npm/Go/RubyGems/Packagist; best-effort via GHSA for CocoaPods/SwiftPM/Debian), and GHSA with CISA KEV cross-reference. Structured skipped-list primitive distinguishes ten canonical clean-skip reasons (7 target-shape: no-apk/no-bundle/no-pkg/no-debian-source/no-elf/no-systemd-unit/no-pe; 3 host-OS-gated: requires-macos-host/requires-systemd-host/requires-windows-host; 1 profile-absent: no-notary-profile) from tool failures. `references/COVERAGE.md` is the single source of truth enumerating every lane, ecosystem, and skip reason. Per-run token-cost accounting; offline-degradation drills for CVE feeds and all eight tool lanes; prioritized markdown report with verbatim-quoted primary-source fixes.
